lessons.title: Arrays & the cost of an operation
lessons.body:
### Start with the representation
A `std::vector<int>` stores elements contiguously. Reading an element by index takes constant time. Searching an unsorted vector may require inspecting every element.

### Count the work
For an input of size n, a single traversal is O(n). Two nested traversals can be O(n²). Distinguish auxiliary space from storage occupied by the input.

### Try it
Write down the time and auxiliary space needed to find the maximum in an unsorted vector. A running maximum needs O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space.

lessons.title: Binary search & loop invariants
lessons.body:
### Narrow the search interval
Binary search works on sorted data. Maintain an inclusive interval `[left, right]` that contains every possible location of the target. Compare the middle element and discard the half that cannot contain the target.

Use `left + (right - left) / 2` for the midpoint. Each iteration approximately halves the interval, giving O(log n) comparisons.

### Edge cases
Test an empty input, one element, a missing target, and targets at both ends. Return -1 when the target is absent. With duplicates, finding any matching index is different from finding the first match.

exercises.title: Find a target in a sorted vector
exercises.prompt:
Implement `find_index` without calling a standard-library search function. Return a matching index, or -1 when absent. Keep the iterative solution to O(log n) time and O(1) auxiliary space.

Use the starter tests, then add tests for an empty vector and a target at each boundary.
hints: Maintain left and right indices for an inclusive search interval.
When values[mid] is smaller than the target, move left to mid + 1.
